item.title: Just 11 survived after a predator introduced to fight garden pests nearly wiped them out: Hawaii’s rare tree snails return to the wild after 33 years
item.description: After years of dedicated conservation work, the O‘ahu tree snail has made a triumphant return to Hawaii's stunning Ko‘olau Mountains. Since rescuing the last of the species in 1991 and breeding them to over 1,000 individuals, conservationists have created a safe habitat that shields them from invasive threats. Despite this success, the long-term survival of these snails remains uncertain, necessitating continuous monitoring and further breeding efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: When London Bridge was rebuilt in Arizona, workers numbered granite stones before dismantling it
item.description: London Bridge has a storied past marked by numerous reconstructions due to various calamities. In a striking turn of events, the City of London sold the iconic bridge to American entrepreneur Robert McCulloch for $2.46 million in 1968. The bridge was carefully reassembled in Lake Havasu City, featuring a hollow core designed to accommodate modern traffic.

item.title: Historic US midterms: Black, Indigenous, Latina & LGBTQ leaders win key races
item.description: The 2026 US midterm elections have led to historic firsts in gubernatorial and Senate races across the nation. Notable victories include the first Black woman governor in US history and the first Native American woman governor. The election of Texas' first Latina governor and Florida's first Black governor also signify progress in representation. Additionally, Minnesota has elected its first woman governor, further enhancing diversity in leadership roles.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: North Korea fires missiles hours after rejecting US accusations over Binance hack
item.description: North Korea recently fired multiple missiles towards its eastern waters, indicating rising tensions with South Korea and the US. This action followed North Korea's denial of involvement in a significant cryptocurrency hack attributed to its hackers by the FBI. Kim Yo Jong criticized US accusations as part of a hostile policy and refused dialogue until it changes.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Washington man loses father's ranch over financial abuse; court upholds $166,698 divorce judgment
item.description: Calvin Evans Jr. had anticipated taking over his father's ranch in Washington, a significant piece of property at the center of his divorce. In the proceedings, Deborah Bunney secured $174,000 for community contributions towards the ranch. However, after being found to have financially abused his father, Evans's inheritance was revoked.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: He tracked down over 60 poachers and followed a blood trail for 1.5 km: Meet Zorba, the dog who protected Assam’s rhinos
item.description: Zorba, a Belgian Malinois esteemed for his exemplary contributions to wildlife conservation in Assam, was instrumental in tracking more than 60 poachers within Kaziranga National Park. His remarkable ability to retrieve vital evidence and follow scent trails showcased the invaluable role of trained dogs in environmental protection. Honored for his unwavering service, Zorba passed away in November 2022, leaving a lasting impact on both his handlers and the conservation community.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 1944, a US Navy serviceman stationed in the Pacific mailed his wife a coconut
item.description: In an extraordinary act of devotion during 1944, U.S. Navy serviceman Raymond sent a carved coconut to his beloved wife, Marie. This unique letter, mailed all the way from Hawaii, bore their names intertwined in a heart, symbolizing their unwavering love. Their enduring marriage of 53 years stands testament to a bond that grew deeper with time.

item.title: Katy Perry faces opposition from more than 360 neighbours over proposed 110-acre California youth camp
item.description: Katy Perry’s proposed Gratitude Canyon youth camp in Goleta, California, is facing opposition from more than 360 neighbours. Residents have raised concerns about wildfire risks, traffic, noise and evacuation access. The singer’s Firework Foundation is defending the project, saying it will provide underserved children with opportunities to explore arts, nature and outdoor activities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US couple finds live Civil War-era artillery shell in basement of newly bought home
item.description: A young couple in Pennsylvania discovered a live Civil War-era artillery shell while clearing out the basement of their newly purchased home in South Connellsville. The object was among belongings left behind by the previous owners. The couple alerted police, who contacted the Allegheny County Police Bomb Squad. Specialists confirmed the shell was live and removed it for proper disposal.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: A butterfly disappeared from Ontario in 1988 and has not been recorded there since
item.description: In an exciting conservation effort, scientists are set to reintroduce the frosted elfin butterfly to Ontario, a species that vanished nearly forty years ago. Adult butterflies and their eggs are being moved from New York for breeding in captivity before their release. The initial reintroduction is planned for spring 2027 in Port Rowan, where habitats have been carefully restored.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: A vampire burial: A Polish woman was buried with a sickle to stop her rising from the grave
item.description: Unveiled by time, Zosia's grave in Pień offers a glimpse into 17th century Polish traditions regarding death and the supernatural. Archaeologists found an iron sickle and a toe-bound padlock alongside her remains, suggesting efforts to prevent her from rising as a vampire. This peculiar burial practice hints at Zosia's affluent background, compelling researchers to dive deeper into her life and the cultural fears that shaped her final resting place.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: US poll results: Democrat Amy Acton defeats Ramaswamy, flips Ohio governor's office
item.description: Dr. Amy Acton has been elected as Ohio's first female governor after defeating Vivek Ramaswamy. This historic victory marks the first Democratic win in the state's governorship in two decades. Acton campaigned on healthcare and affordability while highlighting her challenging childhood. Ramaswamy faced significant backlash for a controversial ad featuring Acton's estranged mother. Acton enters office without prior elected experience amid significant political shifts in Ohio.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: US elections: K Bottoms makes history as first Black woman governor, flips Georgia seat
item.description: Keisha Lance Bottoms has been elected governor of Georgia after defeating Rick Jackson in the recent election. Her victory signifies a historic moment as she becomes the first Black woman to hold this position. Bottoms focused her campaign on economic issues, pledging to expand Medicaid and raise the minimum wage. Jackson's significant campaign spending did not prevent his defeat despite his attacks on Bottoms' record.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Trump jokes he'll move to Israel and become PM if Americans get 'tired' of him
item.description: In a lighthearted moment during a Fox News interview, Donald Trump playfully proposed his candidacy for the position of Israel's prime minister, citing a staggering 99 percent approval rating among Israelis. He went on to declare that by 2026, the US would cease its annual aid of $4 billion to Israel, sparking considerable debate over the implications for military support and relations, coinciding with the midterm elections unfolding in America.

item.title: Who protects those counting America's votes? US election workers face threats amid midterms
item.description: In response to escalating threats and harassment, local government workers overseeing elections in the US are now under heightened security measures. This includes installation of bulletproof glass and emergency panic buttons, alongside training to manage aggressive behavior and suspicious items. The situation is compounded by the departure of numerous election officials, complicating recruitment efforts. Federal authorities remain dedicated to investigating threats to maintain the integrity of the electoral process.
